A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KL-tracing study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. Appendices A–B are retained, and v2 adds Appendix C.

before.justification: Sections 4–6, Tables 2–3 and the qualitative figures report original optical-flow evaluations on DAVIS, Kubric and real-world videos.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, and Appendix C/Table 5 adds evaluations of CoTracker-v3 and AllTracker under a two-frame constraint.

M1.justification: The frozen LRAS model and KL-tracing procedure remain unchanged: Gaussian perturbation, conditioned clean and perturbed predictions, patchwise KL divergence, argmax localization and threshold-based occlusion detection. The revised schematics do not introduce algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use TAP-Vid DAVIS, Kubric and the same qualitative video examples. The added tracker comparison reuses DAVIS and the existing two-frame TAP-Vid First task; it does not introduce multi-frame evaluation or new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–3 are retained. Appendix C/Table 5 adds CoTracker-v3 and AllTracker as evaluated baselines on DAVIS, a limited extension of the comparison suite. DIFT is newly discussed but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The added tracker experiment explicitly restricts normally multi-frame CoTracker-v3 and AllTracker to two input frames and reports AJ, threshold accuracy and occlusion accuracy under TAP-Vid First. This adds a testing configuration for the new baselines; the original experiments' metrics, subset and mask/multiscale settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The RGB-versus-KL sampling analysis, three Cosmos conditioning cases and qualitative examples are retained. Appendix C adds baseline scores under the existing two-frame task, without reporting a comparison against full-context operation or another new ablation or sensitivity experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and mask-averaging descriptions. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 2–3 are unchanged. New Table 5 reports AJ/threshold accuracy/OA of 39.9/58.0/76.9 for CoTracker-v3 and 54.9/66.0/78.0 for AllTracker. KL-tracing's 44.2/65.2/74.6 repeats existing results with rounding; AllTracker leads on all three reported metrics in this constrained comparison.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of perturbation, conditioned prediction and patchwise KL divergence are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs. The revised wording about useful model properties is conceptual qualification, not a changed formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of outperforming state-of-the-art models, including the 16.6% and 4.7% improvements, with being competitive with task-specific models. The three principal contributions remain unchanged, and the introduction retains its state-of-the-art statement, making this a limited narrowing of the headline claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 changes the three model properties from requirements to properties that can improve extraction. The discussion adds an argument about expanding applicability through generative-model training data and explains the point-by-point runtime cost. Appendix C adds an interpretation of AllTracker's robustness to missing intermediate frames; the earlier computational-cost and distillation discussion is retained and expanded.

D1.justification: The reported model sizes, perturbation parameters, mask/multiscale settings, Appendix A method summary and project-access information remain unchanged. Beyond the added evaluation constraint covered under E3, v2 supplies no new implementation instructions, hardware information or code/data availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to AllTracker and DIFT and a 'Tracks from Diffusion Models' discussion distinguishing intervention propagation from feature-based correspondence extraction. It also explains the positioning relative to multi-frame trackers. CoTracker was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main section sequence is retained. V2 edits the abstract, replaces several uses of 'world model' with 'video model', expands related work and discussion, and adds Appendix C. These are localized revisions rather than an extensive rewrite or structural overhaul.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn with revised model blocks, arrows and labels, and Table 5 is added. Existing figures and tables are redistributed across pages, while their substantive visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds relevant modern tracker comparisons and moderates the abstract's broad outperformance claim. Table 5 makes the competitive picture clearer by showing AllTracker ahead on the three reported metrics, while preserving the original method and main results. This improves evidential context and claim calibration, although the added tracker evidence applies only to the explicitly constrained two-frame setting.
